html:
Jerusalem is an ancient city in the hills of the southern Levant, between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea, and a holy city to Jews, Christians and Muslims. - Israel's capital. The Bible says David took the Canaanite town around 1000 BCE and made it capital of the united kingdom, and that Solomon built the First Temple there.

  • Exile and return. Babylon destroyed the city and its Temple in 586 BCE. Exiles came back under Persian rule and built the Second Temple.
  • Rome. Pompey took the city in 63 BCE, and it became the centre of Judea. Herod rebuilt the Temple on a grand scale. Jesus was crucified outside its walls around 30 CE. The Romans destroyed the Second Temple in 70 CE and, after the Bar Kokhba revolt, refounded it as a pagan colony barred to Jews.
  • Christian and Muslim holy city. Constantine built the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in the 300s. Muslim Arabs took the city in about 638, and the caliph Abd al-Malik built the Dome of the Rock in 691.
  • Crusades. The First Crusade took it in 1099 with a massacre; Saladin won it back in 1187.

The Ottomans ruled from 1517 and built the walls that still ring the Old City. Britain took it in 1917. After 1948 it was divided between Israel and Jordan, and Israel took the eastern half in 1967. Both Israel and the Palestinians claim it as their capital.
